{{Use dmy dates|date=December 2020}}
{{Use New Zealand English|date=December 2020}}
'''Joan Muriel Mattingley''' (married name '''Cameron'''; 5 March 1926 – 27 July 2015) was a New Zealand clinical chemist.

Mattingley was born in [[Wellington]] on 5 March 1926,<ref name="Death registration">{{cite web |url=https://www.bdmhistoricalrecords.dia.govt.nz/search/search?path=%2FqueryEntry.m%3Ftype%3Ddeaths |title=Death search: registration number 2015/20377 |website=Births, deaths & marriages onlin |publisher=Department of Internal Affairs |access-date=12 January 2021 |archive-date=22 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180622060259/https://www.bdmhistoricalrecords.dia.govt.nz/search/search?path=%2FqueryEntry.m%3Ftype%3Ddeaths |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Martin"/> and was educated at [[Wellington Girls' College]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://docplayer.net/52390500-Wellington-girls-college-alumnae-newsletter.html |page=7 |title=Obituaries |work=School Ties: Wellington Girls' College Alumnae Newsletter |date=December 2015 |issue=19 |access-date=12 January 2021 |archive-date=14 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210114205609/http://docplayer.net/52390500-Wellington-girls-college-alumnae-newsletter.html |url-status=live }}</ref> When aged 17, she applied to work at the [[Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (New Zealand)|Department of Scientific and Industrial Research]] but was told that girls could not become botanists "because it required tramping".<ref name="Martin">{{Cite book|last=Martin, Paula, 1966–|title=Lives with science : profiles of senior New Zealand women in science|date=1993|publisher=Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa|others=Women's Suffrage Centennial Science Conference (1993 : Wellington, N.Z.)|isbn=0-909010-16-1|location=Wellington, N.Z.|oclc=30080610}}</ref> Mattingley graduated with a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree from [[Victoria University of Wellington|Victoria University College]] in 1949,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://shadowsoftime.co.nz/university15.html |title=NZ university graduates 1870–1961: Ma |website=Shadows of Time |access-date=12 January 2021 |archive-date=18 January 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190118182819/http://shadowsoftime.co.nz/university15.html |url-status=live }}</ref> and completed a [[PhD]] in biological chemistry from [[Victoria University of Wellington]] in 1977.<ref>{{Cite web|title=History of chemistry {{!}} School of Chemical and Physical Sciences {{!}} Victoria University of Wellington|url=https://www.wgtn.ac.nz/scps/about/history/history-of-chemistry|access-date=2020-12-26|website=www.wgtn.ac.nz|date=4 October 2019 |archive-date=18 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211018025620/https://www.wgtn.ac.nz/scps/about/history/history-of-chemistry|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Wellington|first=Victoria University of|date=2019-03-26|title=Prize details {{!}} Scholarships {{!}} Victoria University of Wellington|url=https://www.wgtn.ac.nz/scholarships/annual-prizes/prize-details?result_1736977_result_page=267|access-date=2020-12-26|website=www.wgtn.ac.nz|language=en|archive-date=23 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201023002812/https://www.wgtn.ac.nz/scholarships/annual-prizes/prize-details?result_1736977_result_page=267|url-status=live}}</ref> She worked as a clinical chemist, and rose to become the senior scientific officer in the biochemistry research unit at [[Wellington Hospital, New Zealand|Wellington Hospital]].<ref name="RSNZ"/>

Mattingley was twice president of the [[New Zealand Association of Scientists]] (NZAS) in 1987/88 and 1988/89. During her tenure, the NZAS made many submissions on government restructuring of the New Zealand science system. Mattingley referred to these changes as "extraordinary upheavals" that would devastate New Zealand science and create a "generally confused, bewildered, insecure scientific community".<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Gregory|first=G.|date=2017-02-22|title=Service to science: history of the New Zealand Association of Scientists|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1080/03036758.2017.1291435|journal=Journal of the Royal Society of New Zealand|volume=47|issue=2|pages=175–180|doi=10.1080/03036758.2017.1291435|bibcode=2017JRSNZ..47..175G |s2cid=133339651|issn=0303-6758|access-date=26 December 2020|archive-date=18 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211018025623/https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/03036758.2017.1291435|url-status=live|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Her biography of the scientist [[Brian Shorland]] was published under her married name, Joan Cameron.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Cameron|first=Joan|title=Brian Shorland: Doyen of New Zealand science.|publisher=New Zealand Association of Scientists|year=2014|location=Wellington}}</ref>

Mattingley died in [[Paraparaumu]] on 27 July 2015, having been predeceased by her husband, Charles Cameron.<ref name="Death registration"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://kapiticoastfuneralhome.co.nz/wp-admin/admin-ajax.php?action=wpfh_print_obit&oid=289&obituary=1 |title=Joan (Dr) Cameron (née Mattingley) |publisher=Kapiti Coast Funeral Home |access-date=12 January 2021 |archive-date=13 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210113220524/https://kapiticoastfuneralhome.co.nz/wp-admin/admin-ajax.php?action=wpfh_print_obit&oid=289&obituary=1 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2017, Mattingley was selected as one of the Royal Society Te Apārangi's "[[150 women in 150 words]]", celebrating the contributions of women to knowledge in New Zealand.<ref name="RSNZ">{{Cite web|title=Joan Mattingley|url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/150th-anniversary/150-women-in-150-words/1968-2017/joan-mattingley/|access-date=2020-12-26|website=Royal Society Te Apārangi|archive-date=25 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201125160016/https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/150th-anniversary/150-women-in-150-words/1968-2017/joan-mattingley/|url-status=live}}</ref>
